title: PDF Too Big to Email? Make a Smaller, Readable Copy
description: Check your email attachment limit, compress a PDF copy and inspect small text before sending. Learn when a sharing link is a better option.
direct: Check the sending account and the recipient's attachment rules first. Compress a separate PDF copy, then verify its file size and readability. If it is still too large, share an access-controlled link or send only the pages the recipient needs.
figureAlt: Three checks for an email PDF: check the receiving limit, inspect text and images in a compressed copy, then test the attachment or sharing link.
figureCaption: File size and legibility both matter. This is an explanatory workflow, not an App screenshot.

cards.heading: Know the limit
cards.body: Personal Gmail allows 25 MB of attachments in total. Work or school limits can be set by an administrator.

cards.heading: Check the copy
cards.body: Small text, form fields, signatures and page count matter more than an advertised compression percentage.

cards.heading: Use a link when needed
cards.body: A link avoids a large email attachment, but introduces hosting permissions and access requirements.

sections.heading: Check the whole message, not just one PDF
sections.body: Google lists a 25 MB total attachment limit for personal Gmail and says larger attachments are replaced with a Google Drive link. Work and school account limits may be set by an administrator. Microsoft's Outlook help distinguishes account types and notes that message limits can include the attachment and email itself. The recipient can impose a lower limit too. Read the actual rejection message rather than assuming every provider has the same cap.

sections.heading: Compress a copy in the browser
sections.body: Open our PDF compressor, choose the PDF and start with the Balanced quality option. Compress and download a separate copy. Supported processing runs locally in your browser. Browser PDF exports include a small Just Compress app logo watermark, so check that this is acceptable for your recipient before using it for an application or formal document.

sections.heading: Check the result before attaching it
sections.body: Open the new PDF and compare the first page, the smallest text, diagrams and any signatures with the original. Check page count and file size. Compression can reduce image quality, and an already optimized PDF may barely shrink. Do not promise a fixed percentage or assume that a successful export preserves every document feature. Keep a signed original and follow any requirements for digitally signed files.

sections.heading: If it is still too large
sections.body: Send only the pages the recipient needs if that is allowed, or use a sharing link from an approved service. In Gmail, an oversized attachment may be replaced with a Drive link. In Apple Mail, Mail Drop supports attachments up to 5 GB subject to its service limits. These options upload a copy for sharing. Check recipient permissions and any expiry instead of describing them as no-upload delivery.

sections.heading: On iPhone
sections.body: Our App, PDF Compressor: Sign & Merge, offers PDF compression and related document tools. Check the verified App Store listing below for current purchase options. Export a copy, inspect the actual PDF, then attach it using your mail app. The app name does not establish that every export will satisfy a particular portal or mail server.

steps.text: Check the account, total attachment size and recipient requirements.
Compress a separate copy. Inspect small text, page count and any marks or signatures.
Attach the checked copy, or share an approved link and verify recipient access.

faqs.heading: What size should I target for email?
faqs.body: Use the actual sending and receiving limits, counting all attachments. Leave room under the applicable limit. There is no universal safe size for every account.

faqs.heading: Will PDF compression always make the file much smaller?
faqs.body: No. Image-heavy documents may shrink more than text-heavy or already optimized files. Inspect the actual result and readability.

faqs.heading: Does the free browser PDF tool add a watermark?
faqs.body: Yes. Browser PDF exports include a small Just Compress app logo watermark. Check the output and the recipient's requirements before sending.

title: Video Too Big for WhatsApp? Choose the Right Sending Method
description: Choose between a smaller chat video, a document attachment and a Status clip. Check the current limit, compress a copy and verify what your recipient receives.
direct: First decide how you want to send the video. A chat video, a document attachment and a Status update have different rules. Keep the original, check the limit shown in your WhatsApp app, then make a smaller copy only if you need one.
figureAlt: Three separate paths: a chat video for convenient viewing, a document for sharing a file, or a Status clip with a duration limit.
figureCaption: Choose the delivery type before choosing a compression setting. This is a workflow diagram, not a WhatsApp screen.
cards: Chat video
Best for viewing directly in the conversation. WhatsApp may compress media; pre-compression does not guarantee it will leave your file unchanged.
Document
Best when you want to send a file attachment. WhatsApp currently documents a 2 GB document limit. The recipient still needs to download and play the file.
Status
A separate publishing route. Check the duration and options in Status rather than applying document limits.
sections: Which limit applies?

There is no single 16 MB limit for every WhatsApp video workflow. In its current media help, WhatsApp describes default video limits of 100 MB at 720p for faster connections and 64 MB at 480p for slower connections. It separately lists a 2 GB document limit and a 90-second Status duration. These are contextual limits, not a promise that every version or receiving device accepts every file. Check the current app message and the official help linked below.
Make a smaller sharing copy

Start with a short representative clip. Open our browser video compressor, select the video, choose a quality level and compress. Download the result, check its actual size, and watch a bright area, motion and any on-screen text. If it looks too soft, use a less aggressive setting or shorten only material you do not need. The original should remain your editing copy.
On iPhone

Our App, Video Compressor & MP4 Convert, supports video compression and conversion. Its current App Store listing is linked below for features, device requirements and purchase options. Export a copy, inspect it in Files or Photos, then attach that result in WhatsApp. This page does not claim a particular export will pass every receiving limit.
Still cannot send it?

Read the exact error. A file can be small enough but still have a format, playback or connection problem. Try playing the exported copy locally and test one short clip with the recipient. If you are sharing a document, use the attachment control and choose the document or file option available in your version. A full-size file uses the recipient's storage and data too.
Keep privacy and color separate

Our browser compressor processes the supported clip locally; sending it through WhatsApp is a separate action. If colors change after sharing, compare the original and received copy before treating the problem as file size. The HDR and HEVC guides below explain those different checks.
steps: Choose chat video, document or Status. Read the current limit for that route.
Keep the original. Make one smaller copy and inspect the actual size and playback.
Send a test to the intended destination. Check what the recipient actually receives.
faqs: Does making the video smaller prevent WhatsApp compression?
No. WhatsApp can still process a media attachment. Pre-compression helps control the input size; it does not guarantee an unchanged delivered video.
Is every WhatsApp video limited to 16 MB?
No. Delivery type and current app behavior matter. The current official media help distinguishes connection-dependent media limits, a 2 GB document limit and a separate Status duration.
Why does a small video still fail?
Size is only one check. Inspect the error, accepted format, playback and network connection, then test a short copy.

title: What does no-upload file processing mean?
description: No-upload processing means the selected file operation runs on your device. The webpage still loads software from the internet. Check the file workflow, website analytics and any later sharing step separately.

sections: Three different data flows

Loading a webpage, processing a document and sharing its output are different actions. A local compressor can keep your PDF on the device while the hosting service receives ordinary connection requests. Optional website analytics can record a page visit after consent without receiving the selected file.
What to check before selecting a file

Read where processing happens, what output the tool creates and which limitations matter for your task. A server deletion promise describes uploaded files; a genuinely local operation avoids that processing upload. A private file still needs a secure device and an appropriate sharing destination.
When local processing is a practical fit

Simple compression, trimming, conversion and basic document edits can often run locally. Very large files may exceed a browser tab's resources. Keep the original, try a representative copy and inspect the result instead of assuming every supported-looking extension will work.
What local processing does not guarantee

It does not promise that a site never loads external resources, that a device is secure, or that sending the result through another service stays local. Our website privacy page explains the separate optional analytics controls.

Inspect the exported file

Open the exported PDF. Check page order and count, small text, any visible signature, links and fields that the recipient requires. Confirm the actual file size and try the intended upload or mail workflow before deleting a source copy.

No. File compression changes the encoded file size. Dynamic compression changes level differences in the audio.

title: Technical vs Creative LUTs: Which Comes First?
description: Understand conversion LUTs, creative looks and hybrid LUTs. Match input color spaces, avoid double conversion, and choose the right Apple Log LUT input in VideoFix.
direct: A technical LUT maps a defined input to a defined output. A creative LUT adds a look. Convert first only when the look expects the converted image. A hybrid LUT can do both, so stacking another conversion may give the wrong result.
figureAlt: Matching source Apple ProRes Log and VideoFix Rec.709 SDR frames, showing normalization rather than a creative look.
figureCaption: Matched 2.000-second frames from an Apple ProRes Log source and its VideoFix SDR conversion. This demonstrates normalization, not a custom LUT or creative grade.

cards.heading: Technical: change the encoding
cards.body: Example: Apple Log to Rec.709. The expected camera curve and gamut matter. A Sony S-Log LUT does not become an Apple Log transform just because both images look flat.

cards.heading: Creative: choose the appearance
cards.body: A look may alter contrast, hues or saturation. It still expects a specific input. “Cinematic” is a style label, not an input color space.

cards.heading: Read the LUT’s input before choosing an order
cards.body: For a look designed for Rec.709, the simple chain is Apple Log → matching conversion → Rec.709 look. A look designed for Log belongs at a different stage. Check its documentation instead of assuming every creative LUT comes last.

cards.heading: Why can two LUTs look worse?
cards.body: Some LUTs combine normalization and a look. Feeding that hybrid LUT an already-converted image can exaggerate contrast or clip detail. An editor may also apply camera conversion automatically. Check both before adding another transform.

steps.text: In VideoFix: HDR Video Converter on iPhone, import Apple Log footage and open its Log preview. Import a compatible LUT. Select Original Log for an Apple Log-to-Rec.709 LUT; select Rec.709 when the LUT expects the normalized Rec.709 image.

Compare the same frame, especially bright clouds, skin and deep shadows. Export a short copy and play it back before processing a batch. A LUT is not a substitute for correcting an incorrectly exposed shot.

direct: Choose AAC when the receiving app or device supports it and efficient encoding matters. Choose MP3 when a recipient or older player specifically needs it. Both are lossy formats: keep your original, and judge a short export by listening rather than its extension.

cards.heading: AAC: efficient encoding
cards.body: AAC can preserve slightly more quality than MP3 at a similar file size, depending on the encoder and material. It is a useful listening-copy choice for compatible devices.

cards.heading: MP3: broad compatibility
cards.body: Use MP3 when the destination requests .mp3 or you need a copy for a player that does not accept AAC. Check the actual receiving requirements first.

sections.heading: Will AAC always make a smaller file?
sections.body: No. Duration and total bitrate determine most of the encoded size. Ten minutes at a constant 128 kbps is about 9.6 MB before headers and metadata, whichever codec you choose. AAC efficiency is a quality tradeoff, not an automatic size reduction. For the calculation, see our audio bitrate guide below.

sections.heading: Keep the original before converting
sections.body: Converting AAC to MP3, or MP3 to AAC, cannot recover discarded detail. Another lossy encode can reduce quality. Export from the best available original and listen to speech, music and quiet passages in the copy before sharing.

sections.heading: A desktop option
sections.body: On Mac, Apple Music can convert eligible local files with its AAC or MP3 encoder. That is an alternative if the files are already on your computer. Apple limits conversion of iTunes Store purchases to iTunes Plus songs.

steps.text: On iPhone, import your local recording into Audio Compressor MP3 Converter and choose the available output format. Use MP3 when the recipient requires that extension.
Export a separate copy, check its format and size, and test playback where it will be used. Our App supports audio conversion; its current store listing describes export tools as Pro features.

title: Rec.709 vs Rec.2020: Color Gamut Is Not HDR
description: Rec.2020 covers a wider color gamut than Rec.709, but does not automatically mean HDR. Learn what to check before exporting an SDR sharing copy on iPhone.
direct: Rec.2020 defines a wider color gamut than Rec.709. That means it can represent a broader palette of colors, not that every Rec.2020 video is HDR. Choose an export for the receiving workflow, and check both its color primaries and transfer function.

cards.heading: A bigger palette, not more pixels
cards.body: Rec.709 is the standard-gamut HDTV reference. Rec.2020 uses wider-gamut red, green and blue primaries. These color definitions are separate from your export resolution: selecting 4K alone does not tell you how its colors are encoded.

cards.heading: Why Rec.2020 does not automatically mean HDR
cards.body: Color gamut describes the palette; dynamic range describes the span of brightness. Rec.2020 primaries also appear in Rec.2100 HDR systems using PQ or HLG transfer functions. A primaries label alone is not enough to identify the brightness encoding.

sections.heading: Which should you export?
sections.body: Use Rec.709 SDR when the recipient or editor requests standard SDR delivery. Keep a supported wide-gamut HDR workflow when HDR delivery is required. Converting to a smaller gamut can change colors outside that gamut. Changing a metadata label is not a substitute for color conversion, and exporting Rec.709 footage as Rec.2020 cannot recover colors never captured.

steps.text: For a Rec.709 SDR sharing copy of supported iPhone HDR footage, import the video into our VideoFix: HDR Video Converter and choose Convert HDR to SDR. The published App supports H.264 MP4 output with Rec.709 SDR color.

Keep the original for editing. Export a short copy and check bright areas, saturated objects and playback in the receiving app. Conversion re-encodes the video. The first three conversions are free; unlimited conversions require a purchase.

cards.heading: Same HDR family, different interpretation

sections.heading: Why switching a label is not conversion

cards.body: In a 3000-pixel-wide image with three equal columns, each cell has about 1000 pixels before borders and gaps. A detailed screenshot in that cell cannot retain the full width of its original.

title: Make a Video GIF Smaller on iPhone

cards.heading: Frame count adds up
cards.body: A three-second loop at 10 FPS has 30 frames; at 20 FPS it has 60. Twice as many frames does not guarantee exactly twice the bytes, because image content and compression also matter.

steps.text: Choose a short source clip in Phone Cleaner: Photo & Video and select GIF export.

cards.heading: Check shape as well as pixels
cards.body: A 4 × 6 print has a 2:3 aspect ratio. A differently shaped original needs cropping or borders. Inspect faces near the edges before accepting a crop.

sections.heading: Work the numbers
